encounters.cc: intermittent maroon-colored stools for the past 6 months

lines: Intermittent maroon-colored stools for the past 6 months
This 66-year-old male with poorly controlled Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease returns six months after Internal Medicine visit.
He presents with intermittent maroon-colored stools for the past 6 months and denies abdominal pain, weight loss, or changes in appetite.
His past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes hydrochlorothiazide, and chronic kidney disease stage 3.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 68, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 72
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (30 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month.

Rectal examination reveals maroon-colored stool in the rectal vault.

encounters.cc: 6-month history of slowly progressive lower back pain worse at night

lines: 6-month history of slowly progressive lower back pain worse at night
This 67-year-old with diabetes, hypertension, BPH, and GI bleeding evaluation presents with lower back pain.
He describes the pain as a constant, dull ache that is worse at night and does not improve with over-the-counter pain medications.
He denies any recent trauma or injury.
His past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide, and benign prostatic hyperplasia.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 68, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 72
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (30 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month.
On physical examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the lumbar spine, but no overlying skin changes or masses are noted.
Neurological examination reveals no motor weakness or sensory deficits.
Digital rectal examination shows an enlarged, firm, and nodular prostate.
A lumbar spine X-ray demonstrates several focal sclerotic lesions.

encounters.cc: 3-week history of a non-healing ulcer on the plantar surface of the right foot

lines: 3-week history of a non-healing ulcer on the plantar surface of the right foot
This 67-year-old male with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and peripheral arterial disease, evaluated 8 months prior for suspected prostate cancer, presents for follow-up.
He reports minimal pain, which he attributes to his peripheral neuropathy.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 68, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 72
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (30 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month.
On physical examination, the ulcer measures 2 cm in diameter, with a depth that allows for bone palpation with a sterile probe.
There is minimal surrounding erythema and no purulent discharge. his peripheral pulses are palpable.
Plain radiographs of the foot show cortical irregularities of the metatarsal bones adjacent to the ulcer.

encounters.cc: sudden onset of painless vision loss in left eye described as a curtain coming down

lines: Sudden onset of painless vision loss in left eye described as a curtain coming down

This 68-year-old male with poorly controlled Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, chronic kidney disease stage 3, and peripheral arterial disease, with prior suspected prostate cancer and right foot osteomyelitis, presents with sudden painless vision loss.
He describes it as a "curtain coming down" over his vision.
He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are poorly controlled.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 68, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 72
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (30 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 170/95 mmHg, and his heart rate is 78 beats per minute.
Funduscopic examination of the left eye reveals optic disk swelling, scattered retinal hemorrhages, dilated tortuous veins, and a few cotton wool spots.
The right eye examination is unremarkable.
His fasting blood glucose is 220 mg/dL, and his HbA1c is 9.2%.

encounters.cc: severe constant right upper quadrant pain radiating to right shoulder with fever and chills

lines: Severe constant right upper quadrant pain radiating to right shoulder with fever and chills
The patient is a 68-year-old male with poorly controlled diabetes and recent osteomyelitis and central retinal vein occlusion.
He presents with a 2-day history of severe constant sharp right upper quadrant pain radiating to his right shoulder, accompanied by fever and chills.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 68, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 72
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (30 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month.
His temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), heart rate is 110 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg
Abdominal examination reveals marked tenderness in the right upper quadrant with a positive Murphy's sign.
An abdominal ultrasound shows gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid.
There is no evidence of gallstones.
A plain abdominal radiograph reveals curvilinear areas of gas within the gallbladder wall.

encounters.cc: 2-week history of progressive pain, swelling, and erythema of left lower extremity with foul-smelling heel ulcer discharge

lines: 2-week history of progressive pain, swelling, and erythema of left lower extremity with foul-smelling heel ulcer discharge
This patient has poorly controlled diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, and prior right foot osteomyelitis.
He reports foul-smelling discharge from his heel ulcer present for several months.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 68, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 72
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (30 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month.
His temperature is 38.6°C (101.5°F), blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respiratory rate is 18/min.
Physical examination reveals a 3 cm × 4 cm ulcer on the left heel with black eschar and surrounding cellulitis.
There is no palpable pulse in the left dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial arteries.
Sensation is diminished in both lower extremities.
Doppler ultrasound of the left lower extremity shows no flow in the anterior tibial, posterior tibial, or peroneal arteries.

encounters.cc: sudden onset of severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back

lines: Sudden onset of severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back

This 69-year-old male with hypertension, diabetes, and peripheral arterial disease, hospitalized for limb ischemia, presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe, tearing chest pain radiating to the back.
He describes the pain as the worst he has ever experienced.
- Infected gangrene of lower extremity with nonrevascularizable critical limb ischemia (diagnosed 2023-03-15)
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 68, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 72
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (30 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month.
His blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute.
Physical examination reveals a diastolic murmur best heard along the right sternal border.
His extremities are cool to the touch with diminished pulses in the lower extremities.
A chest x-ray shows a widened mediastinum and an enlarged aortic knob.
Electrocardiogram (ECG) shows left ventricular hypertrophy without ST or T wave changes.
